blocks.content: You built two types of collision detection in this course.
Where the ball hits the paddle controls the bounce angle. A center hit sends the ball straight up. An edge hit sends it left or right at up to 60 degrees:
That is what makes the game feel controllable. The player can aim by choosing where on the paddle to catch the ball.
You detected which face of the brick the ball entered by finding the smallest overlap across all four sides:

const m = Math.min(oL, oR, oT, oB);
if (m === oT) return "top";
The smallest overlap is the face the ball was closest to when it entered. That is AABB collision detection, the foundational algorithm for 2D games.
clampSpeed() kept floating point drift from accumulating across hundreds of bounces. Speed magnitude in, same direction out, capped at the maximum.
